topic.title: Clustering Structure, Robustness, and Evaluation
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Clustering groups observations without a complete set of class labels, but different objectives can produce different legitimate partitions. This topic studies affinities, information preservation, hierarchical structure, robustness to outliers, and evaluation of cluster difficulty. It also examines how learned representations and pseudo-labels interact with the clustering objective.
topic.whyItMatters: A useful partition should match the intended notion of similarity rather than merely optimize a convenient score. Some observations may not belong in any reliable group, and local consistency can conflict with global balance. Understanding these choices makes clustering results more interpretable and less likely to be mistaken for unique natural categories.
topic.evolution: Early representative titles concern conceptual clustering. A 2000 method extracts stable structures from a Markov relaxation using information bottleneck ideas, while 2010 work treats clusters as high-affinity subsets that can leave outliers unassigned. A 2026 short-text method combines neighborhood semantic consistency with global optimal-transport pseudo-labeling.
openQuestions: How can evaluations distinguish unstable partitions from genuinely ambiguous data?
When should a clustering method leave observations unassigned rather than force a group?

papers.tldr: A3S strategically merges and splits initial clusters, improving clustering quality while requiring fewer human pairwise judgments in experiments.

papers.title: Cluster-Aware Similarity Diffusion for Instance Retrieval
papers.tldr: Cluster-Aware Similarity diffusion improves retrieval by restricting similarity propagation to local clusters and smoothing neighboring relationships.

papers.title: MC-GTA: Metric-Constrained Model-Based Clustering using Goodness-of-fit Tests with Autocorrelations
papers.tldr: MC-GTA combines feature similarity and metric autocorrelation in a statistically motivated clustering objective with reported accuracy and speed gains.

papers.title: New Bounds on the Cohesion of Complete-link and Other Linkage Methods for Agglomerative Clustering
papers.tldr: Improved cohesion bounds distinguish complete-link from single-link for diameter approximation and extend to linkage methods including average-link.

papers.title: Efficient Centroid-Linkage Clustering
papers.tldr: A new approximate centroid-linkage algorithm combines dynamic nearest-neighbor search with empirical speedups of up to 36 times while maintaining clustering quality.

papers.title: Expected Probabilistic Hierarchies
papers.tldr: EPH learns distributions over hierarchies using expected objectives that preserve the discrete global optimum values for two clustering scores.

papers.title: Interactive Deep Clustering via Value Mining
papers.tldr: Interactive Deep Clustering improves pretrained clustering models by requesting user feedback on difficult, representative, and diverse samples.

papers.title: On the cohesion and separability of average-link for hierarchical agglomerative clustering
papers.tldr: Theory and real-data experiments support average-link clustering when both within-cluster cohesion and between-cluster separation are important.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithms for Learning Partitions with Faulty Oracles
papers.tldr: The paper gives query-optimal algorithms for exactly recovering groups from pairwise answers despite a bounded number of errors.

papers.title: Query-Efficient Correlation Clustering with Noisy Oracle
papers.tldr: The paper combines adaptive similarity sampling with approximate correlation clustering to obtain polynomial-time guarantees under confidence or query-budget constraints.

papers.title: Unsupervised Discovery of Formulas for Mathematical Constants
papers.tldr: Clustering formulas by their convergence dynamics reveals new expressions for mathematical constants and patterns extending to infinite families.

papers.title: Average Sensitivity of Hierarchical $k$-Median Clustering
papers.tldr: The paper proposes hierarchical k-median clustering with provably low average sensitivity to random point deletion and high clustering quality.

papers.title: Correlation Clustering Beyond the Pivot Algorithm
papers.tldr: Modified Pivot improves correlation clustering through local changes, achieving a provable approximation below three and fewer mistakes in experiments.

papers.title: Generalization Performance of Ensemble Clustering: From Theory to Algorithm
papers.tldr: Generalization bounds motivate a weighted ensemble clustering algorithm that balances base-clustering bias and diversity.

papers.title: Hierarchical Overlapping Clustering on Graphs: Cost Function, Algorithm and Scalability
papers.tldr: The paper introduces an objective and scalable algorithm for graph clusters that are both nested and overlapping.

papers.title: Learning-Augmented Hierarchical Clustering
papers.tldr: Oracle-provided auxiliary information enables efficient hierarchical clustering approximations that overcome known barriers in the learning-augmented setting.

papers.title: Learning With Multi-Group Guarantees For Clusterable Subpopulations
papers.tldr: An online calibration algorithm guarantees performance across mixture-model subgroups without requiring the separation needed to learn the clusters themselves.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Variable Selection in Model-Based Clustering with Missing Not at Random
papers.tldr: A unified clustering framework selects informative variables while modeling group-dependent missingness, with consistency guarantees under regularity conditions.

papers.title: Accelerating data-driven algorithm selection for combinatorial partitioning problems
papers.tldr: The paper establishes when evaluating selected clustering and max-cut algorithms on smaller subsamples can reliably reflect their performance on full inputs.

papers.title: BioArtlas: Computational Clustering of Multi-Dimensional Complexity in Bioart
papers.tldr: BioArtlas clusters 81 bioart works across thirteen dimensions, revealing relationships involving artists, techniques, historical change, and cross-period concepts.

papers.title: Clustering via Hedonic Games: New Concepts and Algorithms
papers.tldr: The paper develops clustering algorithms through coalition games, using friendship and enmity graphs to find locally stable or locally popular groupings.

papers.title: SpEx: A Spectral Approach to Explainable Clustering
papers.tldr: SpEx uses spectral graph partitioning to fit an interpretable decision tree to any given clustering or directly to a dataset.

papers.title: Ultrametric Cluster Hierarchies: I Want ‘em All!
papers.tldr: A suitable cluster tree supports fast, optimal center-based clustering over its hierarchy, with solutions that form additional hierarchies.

papers.title: Beyond Looking Up, Try Looking Around: Harmonizing Global Structure and Local Consistency in Optimal Transport for Short Text Clustering
papers.tldr: Adding semantic neighborhood information to Optimal Transport produces more reliable temporary labels for short text clustering.

papers.title: CHB: A Diagnostic Toolkit for Hardness-Aware Clustering Evaluation
papers.tldr: CHB explains clustering performance through interpretable data-structure fingerprints and evaluations that account for computational constraints.

papers.title: Clustered Influence Functions
papers.tldr: Clustered Influence Functions caches shared computations to make repeated training-data influence queries substantially cheaper.
